proposals.before: When An Lushan rebelled, Suzong pursued him; when the edict arrived, [Siye] immediately led the way, and with the generals cut their arms in covenant, saying: "In every commandery and county we pass, not a hair's breadth may be violated."
proposals.after: When An Lushan rebelled, Suzong summoned him; when the edict arrived, [Siye] immediately led the way, and with the generals cut their arms in covenant, saying: "In every commandery and county we pass, not a hair's breadth may be violated."
proposals.reason: In 肅宗追之, 追 means to summon or recall to court, not pursue in chase; the literal rendering reverses the sense.

proposals.before: He then joined Zhang Hao, Lu Jiong, Lai Tian, the Prince of Wu Zhi, and Li Huan in broadly pacifying the various prefectures.
proposals.after: He then joined Zhang Hao, Lu Jiong, Lai Tian, Zhi the Successor Prince of Wu, and Li Huan in broadly pacifying the various prefectures.
proposals.reason: 嗣吳王祗 is Zhi, the Successor Prince of Wu; the Prince of Wu Zhi wrongly treats Zhi as part of the place-title.

proposals.before: He was then executed.
proposals.after: He then had him executed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 遂戮之 means Lin had the thief executed; the literal makes the wrong party the executee.

proposals.before: Lin had studied the classics in youth, yet his martial gifts were without peer.
proposals.after: Lin had little scholarly learning, yet his martial gifts were without peer.
proposals.reason: 少學術 means deficient in learning, not youthful classical study; the contrast with peerless martial talent requires the negative sense.

proposals.before: Lin studied the classics in youth, yet his martial talent was without peer.
proposals.after: Lin had little scholarship, yet his martial talent was without peer.
proposals.reason: Same error as the idiomatic reading: 少學術 is lack of learning, not study of the classics in youth.

proposals.before: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the posthumous name Martial.
proposals.after: He was posthumously made Minister over the Masses with the posthumous name Martial.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is Minister over the Masses, not Grand Tutor (太傅).

proposals.before: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor; his posthumous title was Martial.
proposals.after: He was posthumously made Minister over the Masses; his posthumous title was Martial.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is Minister over the Masses, not Grand Tutor (太傅).

proposals.before: He earnestly declined the princely title and was made Duke of Liang, then promoted to Grand Tutor.
proposals.after: He earnestly declined the princely title and was made Duke of Liang, then promoted to Minister over the Masses.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is Minister over the Masses, not Grand Tutor (太傅).

proposals.before: He earnestly declined the princely title and was transferred to Duke of Liang, then advanced to Grand Tutor.
proposals.after: He earnestly declined the princely title and was transferred to Duke of Liang, then advanced to Minister over the Masses.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is Minister over the Masses, not Grand Tutor (太傅).

proposals.before: Late in the Tianbao era the emperor renamed him for his merit fighting in Hexi.
proposals.after: Late in the Tianbao era Xuanzong renamed him for his merit fighting in Hexi.
proposals.reason: Chinese names 玄宗; the idiomatic drops the temple name for a generic emperor.

proposals.before: The bandit leader Gao Yu fled to Chenggu; Zhang Xianzheng of the Southwestern Circuit of Shannan captured him and sent him in; all his followers were hunted down and executed.
proposals.after: The bandit leader Gao Yu fled to Chenggu; Zhang Xiancheng of the Southwestern Circuit of Shannan captured him and sent him in; all his followers were hunted down and executed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 張獻誠 is Xiancheng (誠), not Xianzheng.

proposals.before: The bandit chief Gao Yu escaped to Chenggu; Zhang Xianzheng of the Southwestern Circuit of Shannan captured and presented him; all associates were sought out and beheaded.
proposals.after: The bandit chief Gao Yu escaped to Chenggu; Zhang Xiancheng of the Southwestern Circuit of Shannan captured and presented him; all associates were sought out and beheaded.
proposals.reason: Chinese 張獻誠 is Xiancheng (誠), not Xianzheng.

proposals.before: Before long he was also made Deputy Commander and Military Commissioner of the Southwestern Circuit of Shannan, with headquarters at Ziwu.
proposals.after: Before long he was also made Deputy Commander and Military Commissioner of the Southwestern Circuit of Shannan, with headquarters at Zhouzhi.
proposals.reason: 鷫厔 is the place 盩厔 (Zhouzhi), not Ziwu.

proposals.before: After long he was given the additional titles of Deputy Commander and Military Commissioner of the Southwestern Circuit of Shannan, and encamped at Ziwu.
proposals.after: After long he was given the additional titles of Deputy Commander and Military Commissioner of the Southwestern Circuit of Shannan, and encamped at Zhouzhi.
proposals.reason: 鷫厔 is the place 盩厔 (Zhouzhi), not Ziwu.

proposals.before: Huai'en has deceived his men, telling them that Ziyi was killed by court intrigue.
proposals.after: Huai'en has deceived his men, telling them that Ziyi was killed by Chao'en.
proposals.reason: Chinese 朝恩 is the personal name Chao'en, not an abstract 'court intrigue'.

proposals.before: Huai'en deceived his subordinates, saying, 'Ziyi was killed by court favoritism.
proposals.after: Huai'en deceived his subordinates, saying, 'Ziyi was killed by Chao'en.
proposals.reason: Chinese 朝恩 is the personal name Chao'en, not 'court favoritism'.

proposals.before: Lu Sigong, courtesy name Yifan, came from Sanyuan in Jingzhao. Born Jiank, he entered office through hereditary privilege as adjutant of Ye.
proposals.after: Lu Sigong, courtesy name Yifan, came from Sanyuan in Jingzhao. Originally named Jianke, he entered office through hereditary privilege as adjutant of Ye.
proposals.reason: Chinese 始名劍客 is the name Jianke; idiomatic English wrongly truncates it to Jiank and uses awkward Born Jiank.

proposals.before: Lu Sigong, courtesy name Yifan, a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao; his original name was Jiank; through hereditary privilege he became Commandery Adjutant of Ye.
proposals.after: Lu Sigong, courtesy name Yifan, a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao; his original name was Jianke; through hereditary privilege he became Commandery Adjutant of Ye.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise corrupts 劍客 to Jiank instead of Jianke.

proposals.before: Baozhen's son Jian, a palace attendant, concealed his father's death. With his subordinates Lu Huichang and Yuan Zhongjing he assembled the generals; Zhongjing forged an order in Baozhen's name: "My illness prevents me from governing. Jian shall command the army—assist him faithfully."
proposals.after: Baozhen's son Jian, a Palace Attendant Censor, concealed his father's death. With his subordinates Lu Huichang and Yuan Zhongjing he assembled the generals; Zhongjing forged an order in Baozhen's name: "My illness prevents me from governing. Jian shall command the army—assist him faithfully."
proposals.reason: 殿中侍御史 is Palace Attendant Censor, not the vague palace attendant.

proposals.before: Wei Shaoyou, fearing Zai, had long indulged Jia. When Sigong replaced him, he had Jia beaten to death that same day.
proposals.after: Wei Shaoyou, fearing Zai, had long indulged Jia. When Sigong replaced Shaoyou, he had Jia beaten to death that same day.
proposals.reason: Chinese 代少遊 names Shaoyou; idiomatic him obscures the replaced official.

proposals.before: Once I rode alongside his son Ying when a horse bit my shin. I was terrified, but Ying said nothing and went calmly to see his father.
proposals.after: Once I rode alongside his son Ying when a horse bit my shin. I was terrified, but Ying said nothing and forced himself up to see his father.
proposals.reason: Chinese 勉起见父 means he made an effort to rise and see his father; idiomatic English invents calm composure absent from the source.

proposals.before: He later served as observation commissioner of Bin-Fang and of Xuan-She.
proposals.after: He later served as observation commissioner of Fu-Fang and of Xuan-She.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄜坊 is Fu and Fang (鄜州/坊州); Bin (邠) is a different circuit, so Bin-Fang mistranslates the place name.

proposals.before: His son Ying, courtesy name Congzhong, entered office by privilege as a drafting secretary.
proposals.after: His son Ying, courtesy name Congzhong, entered office by privilege as a Gentleman Compiler.
proposals.reason: 著作郎 is the Gentleman Compiler office, not a drafting secretary; the idiomatic title misidentifies the post.

decisions.reason: 肅宗追之 refers to recalling Siye; the following 詔至 and audience at Fengxiang show summons, not pursuit of An Lushan.
嗣吳王祗 is the title 嗣吳王 plus the personal name 祗; 'the Prince of Wu Zhi' wrongly folds Zhi into the title.
遂戮之 continues Lin as agent with 之 as the thief; 'He was then executed' wrongly makes Lin the executee.
少學術 means deficient in learning; contrasted with 武幹絕倫 it cannot mean youthful classical study.
Same 少學術 error in the literal: lack of scholarship, not study of the classics in youth.
贈司徒 is the Three Dukes office 司徒, not Grand Tutor 太傅.
Literal likewise misrenders 司徒 as Grand Tutor; Minister over the Masses is correct.
進司徒 advances him to 司徒, not Grand Tutor 太傅.
Literal likewise misrenders 進司徒 as advancement to Grand Tutor.
Chinese names 玄宗; replacing that temple name with a generic 'the emperor' drops the specified identity.
張獻誠 uses 誠 (chéng); Xianzheng invents a wrong given-name reading.
Literal has the same 誠/政 romanization error; Xiancheng restores the graph.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 山南西道張獻誠禽以獻

decisions.reason: Local 鷫厔 is a graphic variant of 盩厔 (Zhouzhi); ZZTJ records Baoyu moving his garrison to 盩厔, not Ziwu.
Literal likewise misreads 鷫厔/盩厔 as Ziwu; Zhouzhi matches the historical place name.
朝恩 is the personal name Chao'en, not an abstract 'court intrigue'.
Literal likewise invents 'court favoritism' for the personal name 朝恩.
始名劍客 is Jianke; truncating to Jiank and the awkward 'Born Jiank' corrupt the name.
Literal likewise corrupts 劍客 to Jiank; Jianke restores the full reading.
殿中侍御史 is the censorate office Palace Attendant Censor, not a vague palace attendant.
Chinese 代少遊 names Shaoyou; with Zai and Jia also in view, bare 'him' drops that explicit referent.
勉起見父 means he forced himself up to see his father; 'went calmly' invents composure absent from the Chinese.
鄜坊 is Fu and Fang; Bin (邠) is a different circuit, so Bin-Fang mistranslates 鄜.
著作郎 is Gentleman Compiler; 'drafting secretary' misidentifies the office.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0011/r0012 show English Zhang Xianzheng came only from misreading 誠; the personal-name claim must read Zhang Xiancheng while keeping zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
Accepted r0017/r0018 show English Jiank came only from truncating 劍客; the alternate-name claim must read Jianke while keeping zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
Accepted r0017/r0018 require the renamed-from English value to be Jianke, matching restored 劍客, while keeping zh, to, authority, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
